kaps_punt: Persoonlik, daaglikse gebruike wat water besoedel; Fabriek en plaasafval; Afvalwater en hersirkulering van rioolvuil

items.bewering: Elke dag gebruik ons water om onsself en ons klere en skottelgoed te was. Seep en olie spoel dan saam met die water by die drein af.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: SuSanA/EcoSanRes factsheet 8 on greywater (susana.org/_resources/documents/default/2-408-esr-factsheet-8-greywater-en.pdf): household greywater from washing, laundry and kitchens carries soap/detergent residues and fat and oil from cooking.

items.bewering: Rommel soos papier en plastieksakke waai of spoel soms tot in 'n rivier.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: South African Journal of Science (sajs.co.za/article/view/7700) and UJ thesis on macroplastic in the Jukskei, Hennops and Crocodile rivers; Transnet/eThekwini reports on litter carried by stormwater into Durban harbour. Wind action and runoff both carry plastic into rivers.

items.bewering: Water raak besoedel wanneer seep, olie, rommel of ander afval daarin beland.
items.blok: Water wat by die huis vuil word
items.bron: UK Environment Agency 'Yellow Fish' guidance manual (assets.publishing.service.gov.uk) and SuSanA greywater factsheet: oils spread over the surface and cut oxygen, detergents remove oxygen and can be toxic to fish and plants; litter is a recognised pollutant (SAJS river plastics study).

items.bewering: Chemikalieë is stowwe wat mense vir baie dinge gebruik, soos om skoon te maak of om plante beter te laat groei.
items.bron: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary, 'chemical' (noun): 'a substance obtained by or used in a chemical process'; everyday use leans to manufactured products. The lesson keeps only the 'used' half; that is a simplification, not a falsehood, and it fits everything the lesson places under the word (cleaning agents, fertiliser, pesticides, chemicals a factory uses that end up in its wastewater).

items.bewering: Boere gebruik chemikalieë soos plaagdoders om hul plante teen plae te beskerm.
items.bron: US EPA / FIFRA s.2(u): a pesticide is 'any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest'; Food For Mzansi (foodformzansi.co.za) on intensive pesticide use in South African agriculture.

items.bewering: Baie chemikalieë is nuttig, maar hulle kan water besoedel as hulle daarin beland.
items.bron: Lourens River (Western Cape) studies (scholar.sun.ac.za handle 10019.1/75383 and related) recording endosulfan, chlorpyrifos, azinphos-methyl and others in river water after rain; Food For Mzansi on agrochemical contamination of South African surface and ground water.

items.bewering: Bakterieë is piepklein lewende organismes wat jy meestal nie met die blote oog kan sien nie.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: US DOE Joint Genome Institute (jgi.doe.gov) and EurekAlert release on Thiomargarita magnifica (2022): most bacterial cells are about 2 micrometres and need a microscope; a few giant species are visible. 'meestal' is therefore the correct quantifier.

items.bewering: Sommige bakterieë in water is onskadelik, maar ander kan mense en diere siek maak.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: CDC, 'Germs that can contaminate tap water' (cdc.gov/drinking-water/causes/germs-that-can-contaminate-tap-water.html): Legionella, Campylobacter and others in water cause illness; most bacteria are not pathogens.

items.bewering: Helder water kan dus steeds bakterieë bevat wat mense siek kan maak.
items.blok: Bakterieë wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Wyoming Department of Health (health.wyo.gov, 'Don't let germs spoil water, outdoors fun'): 'even waters that look clear and refreshing can contain germs that make us sick'; Hesperian Health Guides: water that looks clean may still carry harmful germs.

items.bewering: Fabrieke gebruik water om produkte te maak en hul afvalwater kan chemikalieë bevat.
items.bron: Water SA (scielo.org.za, wsa v35n3 a07) and Rhodes University repository studies of industrial effluent as a point source of heavy metals and other chemicals in South African rivers and in the Vaal works.

items.bewering: Boere gebruik kunsmis om hul gewasse beter te laat groei. Reën kan kunsmis en plaagdoders van die lande af in 'n rivier of 'n dam spoel.
items.bron: Lourens River studies (Stellenbosch University): rainfall-induced runoff raised pesticide levels in river water and sediment; SRK Consulting on runoff carrying agricultural nitrogen and pesticides into waterways; Food For Mzansi on fertiliser and pesticide runoff into South African rivers and groundwater.

items.bewering: Kunsmis, plaagdoders en afvalwater kan die water in riviere en damme besoedel.
items.bron: Same sources as above; fertiliser runoff causes eutrophication that depletes oxygen in rivers and dams (Food For Mzansi, citing South African researchers); Daily Maverick on industrial and sewage effluent reaching the Vaal Dam.

items.bewering: Besoedeling van huise en fabrieke en plase kan stroomaf vloei na mense en diere verder langs die rivier.
items.bron: Daily Maverick on Gauteng rivers (Jukskei, Klip, Hennops) carrying sewage, solid waste and heavy metals downstream into the Vaal system; Food For Mzansi, 'Urban water pollution threatens SA's rural farming communities' (downstream users exposed).

items.bewering: Riool is die vuil water en menslike afval wat uit huise, skole en ander geboue weggevoer word.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'sewage': 'waste material (such as human urine and feces) that is carried away from homes and other buildings in a system of pipes'; sewage includes greywater and blackwater from homes, schools and businesses. This confirms the CONTENT of the definition only; whether the Afrikaans word 'riool' names this is a separate onseker item below.

items.bewering: Die woord 'riool' beteken die vuil water en menslike afval self (studieblok 'Riool': 'Riool is die vuil water en menslike afval ...'; 'In dorpe en stede loop baie van die riool deur pype ...'; en die begrip 'riool': 'Vuil water en menslike afval wat uit huise, skole en ander geboue weggevoer word.')
items.bron: Sources disagree on the word's sense. Afrikaans Wiktionary (af.wiktionary.org/wiki/riool) defines riool as the PIPE: "'n Pyp wat deel is van 'n stelsel waarop afvalwater afgevoer ... word"; the Dutch cognate is likewise 'sewer, drain' (en.wiktionary.org/wiki/riool); Afrikaans municipal drainage regulations (Namibian gazettes, lac.org.na) use riool/vuilriool for the conduit and 'rioolvuil' / 'rioolwater' for the contents. Against that, current South African Afrikaans news uses riool for the contents ('5 jaar stryd met bure se riool', Oudtshoorn Courant, Nov 2024, where the overflow is the riool). The WAT and HAT entries could not be reached (login required). If the dictionary sense governs, 'baie van die riool loop deur pype' reads as a pipe running through pipes, and the begrip teaches a learner the content sense only. The CAPS bullet itself uses 'rioolvuil', and the lesson already uses 'rioolwater' in the begrip for rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg. A person should decide whether 'riool' stays (colloquial sense) or the lesson uses 'rioolwater'/'rioolvuil' for the contents; this is a word-sense question for the Afrikaans check as much as a fact question.

items.bewering: In dorpe en stede loop baie van die riool deur pype na 'n rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg.
items.bron: Stats SA General Household Survey via Africa Check sanitation factsheet and SAnews: 57% of households had flush toilets connected to the public sewerage system in 2011, higher in urban areas; 'baie van' in towns and cities is accurate and correctly hedged (many rural and some urban households use septic tanks or pit toilets).

items.bewering: Daar word die vuil water skoongemaak voordat dit terug na 'n rivier of 'n ander waterbron gaan.
items.bron: City of Cape Town, Kraaifontein Wastewater Treatment Works (capetown.gov.za): treated effluent is either pumped to users for irrigation or discharged to the river. True as a description of what a works does. Context for the human, not a fault: the DWS Green Drop 2022 report (via Daily Maverick/GroundUp/Circle of Blue) put 334 of 850 municipal works in a critical state and found roughly half of raw sewage not treated to standard, so in many South African towns this does not fully happen in practice. The sentence makes no claim about how well it is done.

items.bewering: Gewoonlik vang groot siwwe eers rommel soos plastiek en lappe uit die water.
items.bron: Northwest Bergen County Utilities Authority process description (nbcua.com) and City of Cape Town Kraaifontein works: incoming sewage is screened first to remove rags and other large debris; screens are rows of steel bars or fine screens. The 'siwwe' mapping holds: a screen catches what is too big to pass and lets water through, as a sieve does.

items.bewering: In groot tenks sak die swaar vuiligheid daarna stadig na die bodem.
items.bron: FAO, Wastewater treatment and use in agriculture, ch. 3 'Primary treatment' (fao.org/4/V9922E/V9922E04.htm): flow velocity is reduced in settling tanks so suspended solids settle to the bottom, removing about half the suspended solids. Note for the human: some South African activated-sludge works (e.g. Cape Town's Kraaifontein) have no primary settling tank and settle solids after the biological stage instead, with only grit removed early; the lesson's order is the conventional one and 'Gewoonlik' opens the sequence, so it is not false.

items.bewering: Nuttige bakterieë eet dan baie van die vuiligheid wat nog in die water oorbly.
items.bron: NBCUA process description: in aeration tanks cultivated microorganisms 'consume suspended organic matter such as food particles, human waste'; City of Cape Town: 'helpful bacteria clean the water in biological treatment tanks'. Mapping of 'eet' holds: the bacteria take the organic waste in as food and break it down. 'baie van' is right, since they do not remove chemicals such as pesticides, and the lesson does not say they do.

items.bewering: Op sommige plekke word die skoongemaakte water nog verder gesuiwer en vir ander dinge hergebruik.
items.bron: News24, 'Sewage keeps taps running in Beaufort West' (2018) and Water360 case study: Beaufort West's reclamation plant has turned treated effluent into drinking water since January 2011; eThekwini Municipality water reuse brochure (durban.gov.za) on recycled wastewater for industry; Cape Town Kraaifontein effluent pumped to users for irrigation.

items.bewering: Werkers hou die aanleg aan die gang, en die pompe en masjiene gebruik elektrisiteit.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: EPA energy-efficiency material for wastewater (epa.gov, eponline summary of EPA fact sheet) and WaterWorld: pumping and aeration blowers are the main electricity users; water and wastewater facilities are often a municipality's largest energy user, up to about 30% of its energy.

items.bewering: Dit neem ook tyd om die water deur al die stappe te kry.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: SSWM glossary on hydraulic retention time (sswm.info) and engineering references: primary settling about 1-2 hours, conventional activated sludge about 4-8 hours, extended aeration 18-36 hours.

items.bewering: Al hierdie werk kos baie tyd, geld en energie.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: EPA / WaterWorld: wastewater plants use roughly 0.8-3% of all US electricity and energy is about 30% of their operating costs; DWS Green Drop 2022: R8.1 billion needed only to restore South African works to basic function.

items.bewering: Daarom is dit beter om water nie in die eerste plek te besoedel nie.
items.blok: Beter om water skoon te hou
items.bron: US EPA, 'Learn about pollution prevention' (epa.gov/p2): 'it's often cheaper to prevent pollution from being created than to clean it up afterwards'; European Environment Agency report on wastewater (via WWD magazine): tackling pollution at source is cheaper than cleaning up. 'In die eerste plek' is an idiom ('to begin with'), not a ranking; recorded here because it contains 'eerste'. No other superlative occurs in the lesson.

items.bewering: Begrip 'besoedel': Om water, lug of grond vuil of skadelik te maak.
items.bron: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary, 'pollute': 'to add dirty or harmful substances to land, air, water, etc. so that it is no longer pleasant or safe to use'. Read alone it is true, and it fits every case the lesson calls besoedeling (soap, oil, litter, chemicals, fertiliser, wastewater).

items.bewering: Begrip 'chemikalieë': Stowwe wat mense vir baie dinge gebruik, soos om skoon te maak of om plante beter te laat groei.
items.bron: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary, 'chemical': 'a substance obtained by or used in a chemical process'. Read alone it is a simplification (it describes chemicals by their use and leaves out chemicals that are only by-products), but nothing in it is false, and every chemical the lesson names (pesticides, fertiliser, cleaning agents, chemicals in factory wastewater) fits it.

items.bewering: Begrip 'bakterieë': Piepklein lewende organismes wat jy meestal nie met die blote oog kan sien nie. Sommige is onskadelik, maar ander kan mense en diere siek maak.
items.bron: JGI/DOE on bacterial size and the visible exception Thiomargarita magnifica; CDC on waterborne pathogens. Read alone it fits everything the lesson puts under the word, including the 'nuttige bakterieë' at the works (which are among the harmless ones).

items.bewering: Begrip 'plaagdoder': 'n Chemikalie wat gebruik word om plae soos insekte dood te maak of weg te hou.
items.bron: US EPA / FIFRA s.2(u): a pesticide is a substance intended for 'preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest'. 'dood te maak of weg te hou' covers killing and repelling; insects are given as an example, not as the only pests.

items.bewering: Begrip 'afvalwater': Water wat reeds gebruik is en daardeur vuil geword het.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary / Dover Township: wastewater is the contaminated water from homes, schools and businesses after use in toilets, showers, washing machines and the like. Read alone it is true and fits both uses in the lesson (factory wastewater and wastewater polluting rivers and dams).

items.bewering: Begrip 'rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg': 'n Plek waar vuil rioolwater skoongemaak word voordat dit na riviere of ander waterbronne teruggaan.
items.bron: City of Cape Town, Kraaifontein works: sewage is screened, treated biologically, settled and disinfected, then discharged to the river or pumped to users. Read alone it is true; the lesson's own note that some treated water is purified further and reused instead does not contradict it, because the entry does not say that all of it goes back.

items.bewering: Die oorsake en die skoonmaakstappe saam gelees: huise (seep, olie, rommel), chemikalieë, bakterieë, fabrieke en plase, en dan die aanleg wat rioolwater met siwwe, besinktenks en nuttige bakterieë skoonmaak.
items.bron: Tested as a set against the NBCUA, FAO and City of Cape Town process descriptions. The set holds: the lesson never says the works receives farm runoff or cleans out pesticides or factory chemicals, never says the returned water is safe to drink, and keeps harmful bacteria (block 3) separate from useful bacteria (block 6) with 'sommige ... ander'. The real final disinfection step (chlorine or ponds, as at Kraaifontein) is left out; that omission makes nothing in the lesson false, because no sentence claims that the three steps remove the harmful bacteria. Sieves catching 'plastiek en lappe' matches the litter named in block 1.

opsomming: Every factual claim, step and definition checked out, including each treatment step and the causes and treatment read together. One point needs a person: the lesson uses 'riool' to mean the sewage itself, but dictionary and technical Afrikaans use 'riool' for the pipe and 'rioolvuil' or 'rioolwater' for its contents (CAPS says 'rioolvuil'), while everyday South African Afrikaans also uses 'riool' for the contents; decide which word to keep. For context, not as a fault: the national Green Drop 2022 report found about half of South Africa's sewage is not treated to standard.
